NDT training in Milwaukee: how it works for Milwaukee employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET to Milwaukee and southeast Wisconsin employers, combining live online classroom sessions with hands-on practical sessions onsite at your plant, foundry or fabrication shop. Your employer certifies you under its written practice after training, documented experience, Level III-administered exams and a vision test.

Milwaukee is a manufacturing city first. Its NDT work comes from foundries and forge shops, heavy equipment builders, pressure-vessel and tank fabricators, power generation, and the shipyards further up the Lake Michigan shore. Much of that work happens inside a quality department rather than in the field, which means the NDT technician is often also a machinist, welder or quality inspector who has taken on a method. For those employers, the SNT-TC-1A model fits well: the company writes a written practice for the methods it actually uses, trains its people to it, and has a Level III administer the exams.

Atlantis NDT has no training centre in Milwaukee. Theory is delivered live online, and practical sessions are run onsite at the employer's facility, on its own equipment and on real production parts or specimens, under ASNT Level III oversight. For a casting or fabrication plant, that means training happens beside the line where the inspection will be done. Request a Milwaukee training quote with your methods, levels and head-count.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Milwaukee

All courses follow the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge. Level I courses prepare technicians to calibrate equipment and perform tests to written instructions under supervision. Level II courses add interpretation and evaluation against codes and customer specifications, and reporting. Level III preparation addresses the basic, method and specific examinations. Recommended classroom and experience hours are defined in SNT-TC-1A and adopted by your written practice; use our training requirements matrix rather than hour figures found elsewhere.

MethodLevelsWhat Milwaukee employers use it forPrerequisite

How the methods map to Milwaukee manufacturing. Foundries and forge shops in the region lean on MT, PT, UT and RT, often to customer specifications and ASTM standards for casting and forging inspection. Heavy equipment builders, including mining and construction machinery manufacturers in the Milwaukee area, weld large structures to AWS D1.1 and customer standards, making VT, MT and UT the core methods. Pressure-vessel and boiler fabricators work to ASME Section VIII and Section I, with ASME Section V governing the NDT methods, which brings RT and UT (including PAUT and TOFD) into play. Power generation and industrial plant maintenance add ET for exchanger tubing and UT thickness surveys.

A typical progression for a Milwaukee quality technician is VT, then MT and PT, then UT, with RT or PAUT for those who move into pressure-vessel or weld inspection roles. The full course list is on the NDT training page. For quality managers who need to run the programme, ASNT Level III preparation is available.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Milwaukee, step by step

  1. Establish or confirm the written practice. Under SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies personnel through its written practice, which sets levels, training, experience, exam content and recertification rules. Many Milwaukee manufacturers already hold one as part of an ISO 9001 or customer-driven quality system.
  2. Complete formal classroom training. Theory, equipment, codes and interpretation for the method and level, delivered live online or in an onsite session. See the training requirements matrix for recommended hours.
  3. Log on-the-job experience. Supervised hours performing the method on production parts. In a plant setting this is often easier to document than in field work, because inspection records already exist; make sure the log is tied to your name and the method.
  4. Pass the general examination. Written questions on method fundamentals, under the authority of a Level III.
  5. Pass the specific examination. Written questions on your employer's procedures, equipment and the codes or customer specifications that apply, such as ASME Section V or casting acceptance standards.
  6. Pass the practical examination. Hands-on testing of specimens or production parts with known discontinuities, graded by the Level III.
  7. Pass the vision tests. Near-vision acuity, repeated annually, and colour contrast differentiation.
  8. Receive written certification. Issued by the employer for each method and level.
  9. Recertify. At the interval set in the written practice, with evidence of continuing competence. Certification does not transfer automatically to a new employer.

For the full explanation, see SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Milwaukee crews

Live online theory. Classroom modules are taught live by an instructor over video, so technicians on first, second and third shift at plants across Milwaukee, Waukesha, Racine and Ozaukee counties can attend without travelling. See online NDT training.

Onsite practical in your plant. Practical sessions are run at the employer's facility using its own equipment, such as wet fluorescent MT benches, penetrant lines, flaw detectors and reference standards, and its own parts. Training on your production parts means the practical training reflects the indications your inspectors will actually see.

Winter and cold-weather planning. Wisconsin winters matter for NDT. Penetrant testing has a standard temperature range under ASME Section V, and outdoor MT and UT work on cold steel has its own practical challenges with couplant and equipment. Onsite sessions for field crews are best scheduled indoors or in warmer months, and we cover temperature limits and qualification of non-standard temperature techniques in the course. Power and process plant clients can schedule training ahead of spring and fall outages. Ask about onsite training for your Milwaukee crew; quotes are usually returned within one business day.

Corporate programmes. Manufacturers training a quality department across several methods can combine theory, practical sessions, exams and written-practice work under a single corporate NDT training programme.

Where NDT technicians work in Milwaukee

Foundries and forge shops. Southeast Wisconsin has one of the country's traditional concentrations of metal casting and forging. Inspection departments use MT and PT for surface discontinuities, UT for internal soundness and RT for casting quality levels, generally to customer specifications and ASTM reference standards. Employers ask for Level II in MT and PT at minimum, and Level II UT or RT for senior inspectors.

Heavy equipment and machinery. Milwaukee's heavy equipment makers, including mining machinery built in the city's harbour district, and a wide supplier base of fabricators and machine shops, weld large structural components. AWS D1.1 governs much of the structural welding, with customer standards layered on top. VT, MT and UT are core; PAUT is growing for high-volume production welds.

Power generation. Wisconsin utilities operate coal, gas and nuclear generating stations, including the Point Beach nuclear plant on the Lake Michigan shore near Two Rivers and large fossil stations in the Milwaukee area. Outage work includes boiler tube, piping, valve and heat-exchanger inspection, generally under ASME Sections I, V and XI-driven programmes set by the owner. Nuclear work carries additional utility qualification requirements.

Shipbuilding on Lake Michigan. North of Milwaukee, Fincantieri Marinette Marine in Marinette builds naval vessels and Fincantieri Bay Shipbuilding in Sturgeon Bay builds and repairs Great Lakes and commercial vessels. Naval shipbuilding follows NAVSEA technical publications and military standards for NDT; commercial work follows ABS rules. Those shipyards set their own qualification layers, but SNT-TC-1A-based method training is a common foundation.

Pressure vessels, boilers and process plants. Fabricators of ASME Section VIII vessels and Section I boilers in Wisconsin need RT and UT capability, and Wisconsin's boiler and pressure vessel programme, administered by the Department of Safety and Professional Services, sets the state inspection context. Food processing, brewing and chemical plants around Milwaukee also run stainless piping and vessels that require PT, VT and UT.

Bridges and infrastructure. WisDOT and regional bridge programmes include steel bridge fabrication to AWS D1.5 and in-service inspection of steel members, drawing on UT, MT and VT.

Radiography licensing in Wisconsin. Wisconsin is an NRC Agreement State. The Wisconsin Department of Health Services, Radiation Protection Section, licenses radioactive material including industrial radiography sources under chapter DHS 157 of the Wisconsin Administrative Code. Radiographers must meet state radiation-safety training and certification requirements, and field radiography at temporary job sites requires at least two qualified individuals. Cabinet and fixed X-ray systems in plants have their own registration requirements. These are separate from SNT-TC-1A method certification. Confirm current rules with DHS before planning RT work.

Level III services and written practices for Milwaukee NDT companies

Manufacturers often inherit an NDT programme that was written years ago, when the plant used fewer methods or a retired Level III ran it. Customer audits, a new aerospace or energy customer, or adding PAUT to the line are common triggers for a rewrite. Atlantis supports Milwaukee employers with:

  • Written practice development and revision, aligned with your quality system. See written practice development.
  • Outside Level III services for plants without an in-house Level III: exam preparation and administration, procedure approval support and records review.
  • NDT procedures and technique sheets for MT, PT, UT, RT, PAUT and ET, referencing ASME Section V, ASTM standards and customer specifications.
  • Audit readiness, checking training records, experience logs, vision tests and certifications before a customer or registrar visit.
  • SNT-TC-1A guidance for quality managers. See SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Book a Level III consultation for your Milwaukee plant.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator gives trainees practice in 12 methods across five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For Milwaukee technicians the NDT lab and welding workshop environments are closest to plant and fabrication-shop work.

It is a practice tool. It helps you rehearse calibration, scanning and interpretation decisions, but it does not replace the practical examination on real specimens and does not count as on-the-job experience.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees course content, examinations and Level III services and supervises onsite practical delivery.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Milwaukee

How do I get NDT certified in Milwaukee?

Work for, or be hired by, an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice. Complete the classroom training, log supervised experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, and pass the vision tests. The employer then issues certification.

Can I take NDT training online in Wisconsin?

Yes. Theory is delivered live online across Wisconsin where the written practice accepts it. Practical training is hands-on and runs onsite at the employer's facility. See online NDT training.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

That depends on your written practice and existing UT Level I record. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum training and experience hours for each level, shown in our training requirements matrix.

Do I need a license for radiography in Wisconsin?

The employer needs a Wisconsin DHS licence for radioactive sources, or registration for X-ray equipment, and radiographers must meet state radiation-safety and certification requirements. Those are separate from SNT-TC-1A certification in RT. Confirm current requirements with DHS.

What does NDT training cost in Milwaukee?

Quote on request, based on method, level, group size, onsite practical needs and any exam or written-practice work. Request a Milwaukee training quote; replies usually come within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Milwaukee employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A-based certification is the common framework for industrial NDT in Wisconsin. Some employers also ask for AWS CWI for weld inspection, NAS 410 for aerospace parts, or ISO 9712 for European customers; Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A only.

Which NDT method is most useful in a Milwaukee foundry?

MT and PT are the everyday methods, with UT and RT for internal quality. Most foundry inspectors hold MT and PT Level II first.

Can PT be done in a cold Wisconsin shop?

ASME Section V defines a standard temperature range for penetrant testing, and testing outside it requires a qualified procedure. The course covers how to handle this. Check your procedure and code before testing in cold conditions.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in Milwaukee?

No. Theory is live online, and practical sessions run onsite at the employer's facility.

Can Atlantis act as our outside Level III?

For SNT-TC-1A programmes, yes: written practices, exams, procedure support and audits. See written practice development.

How can I prepare for ASNT Level III from Milwaukee?

Level III preparation runs live online. Practice questions such as UT Level 2 practice questions help refresh method knowledge.

What do NDT inspectors earn in Wisconsin?

Pay depends on method, level, industry and shift. See the NDT salary guide for what moves pay, rather than unreliable local figures.
